reason: The gap is real and still pre-score: exp89r (56656147) was PENDING at the 08:18Z header, and exp89s/exp89t are not yet submitted. The 08:19Z A-M2 rule (a) sends exp89s whenever d_R >= 0.958. Its V_pub text ('>= 0.960, or 0.959 with an attributable UP over the champion exp87a') assumes that exp87a stays the champion. So if exp89r becomes champion, a tying SEC-free exp89s or exp89t stays behind it under order (1). The 02:02Z rationale (CI has LB '+' reads, SEC only a weak lab prior) does not apply to the pair exp89r vs exp89s. They differ by CI + SEC, and SEC now has a direct LB read of -0.002 (07:59Z). Orders (2) non-CI and (3) fewer levers (5 vs 3) both favour exp89s. A non-CI V_pub also unlocks pair P1 {V_pub, exp75}, which the card's own model rates above P3. The finding overstates one point: its E[exp89r - exp89s] = -0.001 is an unconditioned prior. A true, unmasked k = 0 in a dense block is weak public evidence that exp89s <= exp89r. The swap is justified by private robustness (drop the lever with a negative LB read, fewer levers), not by the public expectation, and the logged text should say so. Reachability is low. d_R >= 0.9595 needs DIS of about +0.0025 (P ~5-10% against a ~0 prior); a same-display tie then has P ~40-50%; if exp89s is higher unrounded, k >= 1 usually swaps already. That puts the material cell at ~1-3%. The 0.959+UP sub-branch depends on how PC36-01 is resolved. Feasibility is trivial: a text line, 0 Kaggle calls, 0 GPU, before the ~09:20-09:35Z read.
